data.narrative: Devanshi demonstrated elite mastery in multi-agent parallel execution planning and interface contract design. Established an isolated branch topology with intermediate checkpoint synchronization points. Designed comprehensive interface contracts specifying UUID standards, ISO 8601 UTC datetimes, and strict error shapes. Systematically diagnosed and resolved subtle contract drift (Unix epoch integers vs ISO strings, and enum casing divergence) before merge, establishing automated CI contract testing safeguards.

dimension_scores.observation: Extracted foundational wire contracts including primitive type constraints, timezone standards, and atomic reservation mutex semantics across 3 parallel streams.
Identified clean Day-1 parallelization between availability, booking, and frontend streams while designating precise synchronization checkpoints.
Anticipated high-risk integration seams (timestamp format mismatches, enum casing drift) and instituted pre-merge contract assertion suites.
Drafted unambiguous interface contracts leaving zero room for subjective agent assumptions on datetime formats, error shapes, and status codes.
Quickly diagnosed rogue agent contract violations through systematic field-by-field diffing and enforced producer-side conformance.
Recognized that changing canonical wire standards introduces widespread client churn, decisively fixing rogue agent output rather than destabilizing consumers.

strengths: Systematic field-by-field contract diffing catching subtle data type drift
Decoupled multi-agent execution topology with clear sync checkpoints
Comprehensive preventative controls including OpenAPI code generation and CI consumer-driven contract testing
